newsitem.title: USA: Mass Port Authority okays ex-US Rep Blute as chief.
newsitem.headline: Mass Port Authority okays ex-US Rep Blute as chief.

text.p: The Massachusetts Port Authority Board voted on Tuesday to approve the selection of congressman Peter Blute as the authority's new executive director. Blute succeeds Stephen Tocco, who resigned earlier this month.
The appointment comes just weeks after the 40-year-old Shrewesbury Republican lost his re-election bid.

Massport owns and operates Boston's Logan Airport, the Post of Boston, the Tobin Bridge and Hanscom Field. Legislators who must come up with the state's 15 percent share of the Central Artery/Third Harbor Project, estimated to cost $10.7 billion, have been eyeing Massport funds as a possible revenue source.
Standard & Poor's Corp rates Massport's revenue bonds at AA-minus on development watch, while Moody's Investors Service has them at a Aa rating.

During the 104th Congress, the two-term representative served on the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee and used his committee assignment to advance infrastructure projects in Massachusetts, according to his official biography.
